title: RESP grant catch-up: what you can get back after a skipped year, and when it's gone
made_by: 엔진/find.py 2026-11-04 · 신호 ['sa2adc239'] · 퍼스나 The late starter

fact.thing: basic CESG grant room per year
fact.claim: The basic CESG pays 20% of what you put into an RESP, up to $500 a year on the first $2,500. If you skip a year, that $500 of grant room is not lost right away. It carries forward, but you can claim at most $1,000 of CESG in one year, on a $5,000 contribution, so you catch up one missed year at a time. The lifetime maximum is $7,200 per child, and grant room only lasts until the end of the year the child turns 17, which means unused room you haven't caught up by then is gone, and a child aged 16 or 17 only qualifies if certain contributions were made by the end of the year they turned 15.

sources.label: CRA: CESG
sources.what: No matter what your family income is, ESDC pays an amount of Canada Education Savings Grant (basic CESG) of 20% of annual personal contributions you make to all eligible RESPs for a qualifying beneficiary to a maximum CESG of $500 in respect of each beneficiary ($1,000 in CESG if there is unused grant room from a previous year), and a lifetime limit of $7,200.

plain.what: An RESP is a savings account for a kid's school. When you put money in, the government adds 20% on top, up to $500 a year on the first $2,500. If you skip a year, that $500 is not lost right away, but you can only make up one missed year at a time, and that takes $5,000 in to get $1,000 added.
plain.so_what: The government can add up to $7,200 per kid over the years, and whatever you have not caught up by the end of the year your kid turns 17 is gone for good.
plain.do: Write down your kid's age today and count how many years are left before the end of the year they turn 17.
